items.title: Posterizarr Plugin for Emby
items.text:
Middleware for asset lookup. Maps local assets to library items as posters, backgrounds, or titlecards.

Port & Credits

This plugin is an Emby port of the original Posterizarr Jellyfin Plugin by fscorrupt. All credit for the original idea, architecture, and implementation goes to him.

This port was vibecoded using Claude (Anthropic).

items.title: Overview
items.text:
The Posterizarr Plugin acts as a local asset proxy for Emby. It is designed to work alongside the Posterizarr automation script, allowing your media server to utilize locally generated or managed assets (posters, backgrounds, title cards) as metadata.

For supported native overlays, Posterizarr can upload directly to Emby. Plex mirroring is optional, not a prerequisite for overlays. Keep local-image sync, direct overlay uploads, and Plex mirroring scoped so they do not compete over the same artwork.

Middleware purpose

This middleware does not allow you to browse, search, or download assets. Its sole purpose is to replace the default artwork by mapping library items to your local file system.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Local Asset Mapping: Maps local files to library items without replacing original metadata permanently in some configurations.
  • Metadata Provider: Registers as a metadata provider for images.
  • Support for Multiple Asset Types: Handles Posters, Backgrounds, Seasons, and Title Cards.
  • Real-Time WebSocket Sync: Connects directly to Posterizarr's event stream. Automatically refreshes Emby library items immediately when artwork is created, edited, or overlay-processed in Posterizarr.
  • Optional Plex Artwork Mirroring: Mirrors active Plex artwork into Emby for movies, TV series, seasons, episode title cards, and backdrops. Detects changes via Plex artwork version timestamps, independently of which tool produced it.
  • Hybrid Sync (Combined Real-Time & Plex Sync): Run real-time WebSocket sync and Plex Direct Sync together. New Posterizarr artwork applies via events, while scheduled Plex sync runs replace it whenever the selected Plex artwork differs.
  • Scheduled Sync Task: Registers a background task to keep library images in sync with your local assets automatically on a customized schedule.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
Optional Plex artwork source

Enable Plex Direct Sync only when Plex should be the source of artwork for this workflow. It can mirror Posterizarr's native overlay results or other selected Plex artwork. Direct native uploads to Emby do not require this option.

  1. Download the latest version of Posterizarr.Plugin.Emby.dll from the GitHub Releases.
  2. Copy Posterizarr.Plugin.Emby.dll into your Emby Server's plugin directory:
    • Docker: /config/plugins/
    • Windows: %appdata%\Emby-Server\programdata\plugins
  3. Restart your Emby Server.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
1. After restarting, go to Dashboard → Plugins → Installed Plugins and click Posterizarr Emby.
  2. Click on Settings.
  3. Configure your Root Asset Folder Path (the directory where your curated images are stored, e.g., /assets).
  4. Image Target Types: Select which artwork types to automatically apply (Posters, Season Posters, Titlecards, Backdrops, Thumbnails).
  5. Real-Time Sync (WebSocket) Settings:
    • Enable Real-Time Sync (WebSocket): Check this box to enable instant updates.
    • Posterizarr URL: Enter your Posterizarr server URL (e.g., http://192.168.1.50:8000 or http://localhost:8000).
    • Posterizarr API Key (Required): Enter your Posterizarr API key. The key is transmitted securely via the X-API-Key HTTP header and is mandatory for WebSocket authentication.
  6. Plex Direct Sync Settings (Optional):
    • Enable Plex Direct Sync: Check this box to mirror artwork directly from Plex.
    • Plex Server URL: Base URL of your Plex server (e.g., http://192.168.1.50:32400).
    • Plex Token: Your Plex authentication token (X-Plex-Token).
    • Libraries to Sync (Optional): Comma-separated list of Plex libraries to sync, or leave blank for all.
    • Artwork Types: Choose which artwork types to mirror (Posters, TV Shows, Seasons, Titlecards, Backdrops).
  7. Click Save.
  8. Go to your Dashboard → Libraries.
  9. Manage a library (e.g., Movies).
  10. Enable Posterizarr under the Image Fetchers settings.
  11. Ensure it is prioritized according to your preferences.
  12. Refresh metadata (Search for missing metadata → Replace existing images) for your library to pick up local assets for the first time.

items.title: Combining Real-Time Sync & Plex Direct Sync (Hybrid Mode)
items.text:
You can enable both Real-Time Sync and Plex Direct Sync simultaneously to get the best of both worlds:

flowchart TD
    subgraph Instant["1. Instant Real-Time Sync"]
        A[Posterizarr finishes rendering] -->|WebSocket event| B[Emby Plugin applies artwork immediately]
        B --> C[Plex sync cache invalidated for item]
    end

    subgraph Scheduled["2. Scheduled Plex Direct Sync"]
        D[Scheduled Plex Sync runs] --> E{Compare Plex artwork with Emby}
        E -->|Different artwork| F[Plex sync wins: applies selected Plex artwork]
        E -->|Identical| G[Skips re-save & updates cache]
    end

    Instant -.-> Scheduled
  • Instant Updates: You don't have to wait for a daily or scheduled Plex sync task to see fresh artwork in Emby. The WebSocket listener updates Emby immediately upon rendering.
  • Plex Source Priority: When the scheduled Plex Sync task runs, the selected Plex artwork takes precedence, including artwork produced by native Dynamic Overlays or another uploader. Identical artwork avoids redundant downloads and disk writes.

items.title: Local Collection Syncing in Plex Sync Mode
items.text: Since Plex Direct Sync only mirrors movie, show, season, title card, and backdrop artwork (Plex does not sync collection artwork directly), Collections are managed locally: * When Enable Plex Direct Sync is active, the Update Collections checkbox remains active and selectable, while movie and TV checkboxes are disabled to prevent overwriting Plex artwork. * The scheduled Posterizarr Sync Task will automatically restrict its run exclusively to Collections (BoxSets). * Image lookup is strictly confined to collection asset directories (Collections/, Collections/<Library>, <Library>/Collections), bypassing individual media folders.

items.title: Real-Time Synchronization (WebSocket)
items.text: The Emby plugin includes a real-time event listener service (PosterizarrWebSocketListener) that connects directly to Posterizarr's /ws/events WebSocket endpoint.

items.title: How It Works
items.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Engine as Posterizarr Engine / WebUI
    participant Backend as Posterizarr Backend (/ws/events)
    participant Plugin as Emby Plugin
    participant Emby as Emby Media Server

    Engine->>Backend: Render Asset / Upload / Replace Artwork
    Backend-->>Plugin: WebSocket event: "asset_updated"
    Plugin->>Plugin: Validate path & confine to Asset Root (CWE-22)
    Plugin->>Emby: Lookup item & SetImage(...)
    Plugin->>Emby: UpdateItem (Instant Refresh)
  1. Instant Event Broadcast: Whether artwork is generated during automated runs (Tautulli Recently Added, Sonarr/Radarr webhooks, manual runs, scheduled runs) or replaced in the WebUI, LogsWatcher detects the change and immediately broadcasts an asset_updated event over /ws/events.
  2. Direct Image Application: Upon receiving the event, the Emby plugin directly opens the rendered file from disk and applies it to the library item via Emby's internal SetImage and UpdateItem APIs. The item refreshes in under a second without requiring a full library scan or waiting for scheduled tasks.
  3. Autonomous Operation: Even if Posterizarr is configured with UsePlex: true and UseJellyfin: false / UseEmby: false, the Emby plugin operates autonomously by monitoring the shared /assets directory. When an asset is modified, Emby updates instantaneously without waiting for the daily scheduled task.
  4. Smart Cache Synchronization: Once an item is updated via real-time sync, its hash is updated in the plugin's SyncCacheManager, ensuring scheduled tasks skip it without redundant re-processing.

items.title: Security Highlights
items.text:
• Strict Header-Based Authentication: The API key is never passed in the URL or query parameters. It is transmitted securely via the X-API-Key HTTP header during the WebSocket upgrade handshake, preventing accidental disclosure in web server access logs or proxy headers.
  • Path Traversal Protection (CWE-22): All event paths are strictly sanitized against directory traversal sequences (..), invalid characters, and rooted paths, and are cryptographically verified to reside within the canonical AssetFolderPath root boundary before any file operation takes place.
  • DoS & Buffer Protections (CWE-400): Incoming frames are enforced with maximum message limits (64 KB) to avoid memory exhaustion.

items.title: Scheduled Tasks & Automation
items.text: The plugin registers a scheduled background task (default: daily at 02:00 AM) that automatically syncs and refreshes your libraries against local assets.

items.title: Configuring the Sync Schedule
items.text:
1. Open your Emby Dashboard.
  2. In the left sidebar under the Server section, navigate to Scheduled Tasks.
  3. Locate the Posterizarr Sync Task in the list.
  4. Click on the task to customize its triggers:
    • You can configure the task to run on an interval, at a specific time of day (e.g., daily at 3:00 AM), on system startup, or on a weekly schedule.
  5. You can also trigger the task manually at any time by clicking the Play (Run) button next to it.

items.title: Building from Source
items.text:
If you prefer to compile the plugin yourself from source code, run:

dotnet publish modules/Posterizarr.Plugin.Emby/Posterizarr.Plugin.Emby.csproj -c Release -o publish

The compiled Posterizarr.Plugin.Emby.dll will be located inside the publish/ directory.

items.title: 🚀 API Endpoints
items.text:
The following API endpoints are available.

Authentication: - Option 1 (Recommended): Add ?api_key=YOUR_KEY to the URL. - Option 2: Use the X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY header. - Option 3: Use Basic Authentication (username/password). - http://admin:posterizarr@YOUR_IP:8000/api/webhook/tautulli

items.title: Overlay Bundles
items.text:
Endpoint Purpose GET /api/dynamic-overlays/bundle/export Download custom YAML and required custom assets/fonts plus layouts and portable settings. Official downloadable Kometa files are dependency references, not ZIP payloads. Credential fields and media-server connections are excluded; known credentials in text are masked. POST /api/dynamic-overlays/bundle/preview Multipart file upload. Returns source profiles, existing destination libraries/server, features, file counts, conflicts, and warnings without applying the bundle. POST /api/dynamic-overlays/bundle/import Multipart upload with file, JSON-string mapping, JSON-string anime_libraries/season_libraries, and boolean import_settings/replace_files. Applies validated mappings and starts in Dry Run, without uploading artwork.

mapping maps source profile names to existing destination library names, for example {"Source TV":"My Shows","Source Movies":""}. An empty value skips a profile. The two feature-target arrays contain mapped destination show-library names. Duplicate destinations, nonexistent libraries, and movie/show mismatches are rejected. replace_files=true explicitly approves conflicting shared files; existing files are backed up before replacement.

Local credentials and media-server selections are preserved even if an uploaded bundle contains credential fields with blank/null/masked values. Invalid bundles return 400; validation failures include detail.code and a readable detail.message so clients can translate the error. Preview responses also include warning_codes alongside the existing readable warnings list. An active sync/classification/import returns 409. See the bundle workflow and limits.

official_dependency_count in the preview reports omitted downloadable defaults. Export returns 503 with code officialCatalogUnavailable if the official Kometa catalog cannot be verified; it does not silently export the whole catalog.

items.title: POST /api/dynamic-overlays/sync
items.text:
Starts a background overlay sync. Without target_items, library and target_server select the libraries and servers to scan. scope: "incremental" skips unchanged artwork; scope: "all" forces uploads.

For an item-only request, supply its media-server ID, server, and library:

{
  "target_server": "plex",
  "scope": "incremental",
  "library": "Kids Shows",
  "target_items": [
    {
      "id": "12345",
      "server_type": "plex",
      "library_name": "Kids Shows",
      "media_type": "show"
    }
  ]
}

ID targets are fetched directly, without listing unrelated libraries. Missing targets are skipped rather than falling back to a broad scan. An empty target_items list does not start a sync. Use jellyfin or emby and the corresponding item IDs for those servers.

A show target also evaluates its season posters and titlecards. Tautulli and Arr notifications submit the movie/show IDs and libraries processed by their trigger run. Requests received while a sync is running are rejected, not queued.

items.title: /api/assets/overview/page
items.text:
Returns only the visible Action Center rows, plus category counts, type/library filter options, and the configuration used to display issue tags.

  • limit: 1-500 rows (default 25); offset: zero-based starting row (default 0).
  • tab: active (default) or skipped.
  • status: Unresolved (default), Resolved, or All.
  • category: a category key from /api/assets/overview, or empty for all categories.
  • search: case-insensitive title/root-folder search; asset_type and library: exact filters.
  • all_matches=true: return the complete filtered set for an explicitly confirmed bulk action. Normal browsing does not use this option.

total_count counts all filtered matches, not just returned rows. offset is adjusted to the last available page if necessary. Category counts and filter options remain independent of pagination. The backend still classifies the full metadata snapshot; this endpoint limits serialization and transfer, not the underlying database read. The original full overview endpoint remains available.

items.title: /api/recent-assets
items.text:
Returns recently modified assets with existing artwork. The dashboard requests only its visible page using limit (1-100, default 100), offset (default 0), and tab (All, Posters, Collections, Backgrounds, Seasons, or TitleCards). The latest 100 matching records are deduplicated before tab filtering and pagination. total_count is the selected tab's count; counts contains counts for all tabs. An offset beyond the available entries is adjusted to the last page. Asset metadata is still matched against the in-memory file cache to preserve modification-time ordering; pagination limits the response, not the database scan.

View Response

  "success": true,
  "assets": [],
  "total_count": 0,
  "offset": 0,
  "counts": {

    "Backgrounds": 0,
    "Seasons": 0,
    "TitleCards": 0

}

items.text: Save the generated collection poster locally in the Assets directory.

items.text: Upload a poster directly to the connected Media Server (Plex, Jellyfin, Emby).

items.title: POST /api/media-server/collections
items.text: Fetch collections directly from the configured media server. When querying Plex, collections are automatically enriched with local asset diff tracking (syncStatus: synced, update_available, missing_server, missing_local), local image URLs (local_asset_url), and disk paths (local_asset_path).

items.title: POST /api/plex/collections/push-item
items.text:
Uploads a single local collection poster directly to Plex via PMS REST API and updates the local push cache database (database/plex_push_cache.db).

View Request 
{
  "rating_key": "12345",
  "local_path": "/assets/Collections/Star Wars Collection.png",
  "url": "http://192.168.1.50:32400",
  "token": "plex-token",
  "title": "Star Wars Collection"
}
View Response 
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Pushed poster for 'Star Wars Collection' to Plex",
  "rating_key": "12345",
  "status": "synced"
}

items.title: POST /api/plex/collections/push-batch
items.text:
Concurrently uploads multiple out-of-sync collection posters to Plex. Uses a controlled concurrency semaphore to prevent overwhelming the Plex Media Server.

View Request 
{
  "items": [
    {
      "rating_key": "12345",
      "local_path": "/assets/Collections/Star Wars Collection.png",
      "title": "Star Wars Collection"
    }
  ],
  "url": "http://192.168.1.50:32400",
  "token": "plex-token"
}
View Response 
{
  "success": true,
  "total": 1,
  "pushed": 1,
  "failed": 0,
  "results": [
    {
      "rating_key": "12345",
      "title": "Star Wars Collection",
      "status": "synced"
    }
  ]
}

items.title: POST /api/plex/sync/run
items.text:
Triggers an on-demand, lightweight background Plex artwork sync in Python (without invoking PowerShell). Scans for modified or missing assets according to specified library and asset types, pushes them to Plex, and writes execution logs to UILogs/PlexSync.log.

View Request 
{
  "library": "all",
  "asset_types": ["collection", "poster", "season", "titlecard", "background"]
}

{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Plex sync started in background",
  "library": "all",
  "asset_types": ["collection", "poster", "season", "titlecard", "background"]
}

items.title: GET /api/proxy/poster
items.text: Proxies local or remote poster images to provide secure previews and avoid CORS restrictions.

items.title: POST /api/media-server/items
items.text:
Fetch paginated items from a connected media server (Plex, Jellyfin, Emby) with clearLogo presence detection and proxied image URLs.

View Request 
{
  "server_type": "plex",
  "url": "http://192.168.1.50:32400",
  "token": "plex-token-here",
  "library_id": "1",
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 50
}

items.title: POST /api/media-server/check-logos
items.text: Batch checks a list of item IDs (rating_keys) against Plex to verify which items already have clearLogo artwork.

items.title: GET /api/media-server/image
items.text: Securely proxies image streams directly from Plex, Jellyfin, or Emby servers without exposing authentication tokens in frontend image URLs. Features persistent local disk caching (Cache/server_thumbs/) and public HTTP cache headers (Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800) to eliminate redundant server polling and optimize UI load speeds.

items.title: POST /api/media-server/upload-logo
items.text: Downloads a selected logo (from URL or data URI), applies Posterizarr metadata tags using Pillow/ImageMagick, and uploads it directly to the media server as a clearLogo.

items.title: POST /api/media-server/collections
items.text: Fetches collections from the media server with diff status detection (Plex) comparing local collection assets against server artwork. Returns syncStatus (synced, update_available, missing_server, missing_local), localPosterUrl, and server poster URLs.

items.title: POST /api/plex/collections/mark-synced
items.text: Marks a local collection poster as In-Sync with Plex in the persistent SQLite cache (database/plex_push_cache.db) without performing a re-upload, updating the status badge immediately.

items.title: POST /api/plex/collections/push-item
items.text: Pushes a local collection poster or backdrop directly to Plex Media Server via REST API (/library/metadata/{rating_key}/posters or /arts) and records the updated timestamp and size in the cache.

items.title: POST /api/plex/collections/push-batch
items.text: Batches multiple collection poster pushes to Plex with rate limiting and concurrency management.

items.title: POST /api/plex/sync/run
items.text: Triggers an on-demand background Plex Push Sync job across configured libraries and asset types.

items.title: GET /ws/events
items.text:
Status probe endpoint for the real-time WebSocket event stream. Used by the Jellyfin and Emby plugin configuration pages to verify network reachability and validate the API key before establishing a persistent WebSocket connection.

Authentication: - Requires X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY or Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY HTTP header.

View Response 
{
  "status": "online",
  "websocket": true,
  "endpoint": "/ws/events",
  "version": "2.0",
  "authenticated": true
}

items.title: WebSocket /ws/events
items.text:
Real-time event bridge for media server integration plugins (Jellyfin and Emby). Dispatches instantaneous notifications whenever artwork is created, uploaded, replaced, or processed with overlays (both from background script runs and manual WebUI operations).

Authentication: - Strictly via X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY or Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY HTTP headers during the WebSocket upgrade handshake (API keys in URL query parameters are rejected).

Supported Events: - connected: Sent upon successful handshake connection. - ping: Sent periodically to keep connections alive (client replies with pong). - asset_updated: Dispatched when an asset is modified, newly created, or overlay processing completes.

View Event Payload (asset_updated) 
{
  "event": "asset_updated",
  "library_name": "Movies",
  "folder_name": "Inception (2010) [tmdb-27205]",
  "asset_type": "poster",
  "season_number": null,
  "episode_number": null,
  "title": "Inception",
  "relative_path": "Movies/Inception (2010) [tmdb-27205]/poster.jpg",
  "timestamp": "2026-09-10T07:12:00Z",
  "libraryName": "Movies",
  "folderName": "Inception (2010) [tmdb-27205]",
  "assetType": "poster",
  "seasonNumber": null,
  "episodeNumber": null,
  "relativePath": "Movies/Inception (2010) [tmdb-27205]/poster.jpg"
}

items.title: POST /api/internal/asset-event
items.text:
Internal event ingestion endpoint for triggering real-time asset updates to connected media servers.

Authentication: - Bypassed for loopback connections (127.0.0.1, ::1) or requires standard API key authentication.

View Request Body 
{
  "library_name": "Movies",
  "folder_name": "Gladiator II (2024)",
  "asset_type": "poster",
  "relative_path": "Movies/Gladiator II (2024)/poster.jpg",
  "title": "Gladiator II"
}

items.title: WebSocket /ws/logs
items.text: Streams live execution logs line-by-line directly to the Web UI terminal viewer (LogViewer.jsx).

items.title: WebSocket /ws/status
items.text: Broadcasts live system metrics, background execution states, and queue progress to the UI.

items.title: Plex: Secure Connection Issues
items.text:
Question: I changed my Plex server to "Secure connections: Required" and now Posterizarr cannot reconnect. I tried using the server's IP address and port, but it doesn't work. What should I do?

Answer: When you require secure connections in Plex, you can no longer connect using a plain IP address because the SSL certificate is tied to a specific Plex domain name.

To fix this, you must use your server's exact, secure domain name. This is a long string that looks something like this: https://192-168-1-50.abcdef1234567890.plex.direct:32400

items.title: How to find your secure Plex URL:
items.text:
1. Open your browser and navigate to the following URL (replace YOUR_TOKEN_HERE with your actual Plex token): https://plex.tv/api/resources?includeHttps=1&X-Plex-Token=YOUR_TOKEN_HERE
  2. Look for the <Connection> tag that has protocol="https" and local="1".
  3. Copy the value of the uri attribute. It should look like the plex.direct example above.
  4. Use this full URI as your Plex URL in the Posterizarr configuration.

Finding your Plex Token

If you don't know how to find your Plex token, refer to the official Plex documentation.

items.title: UI: Action Center Alerts
items.text:
Question: I just setup Posterizarr and I'm getting a lot of errors/alerts in my Action Center. What do I do with these?

Answer: Don't worry! These aren't system errors. The Action Center is simply a list of assets (posters, backgrounds, etc.) that Posterizarr thinks you might want to review.

Common reasons for alerts include: * A poster was found but in a different language than your preferred one. * An image was sourced from a secondary provider (like Fanart.tv) instead of your primary one (like TMDB). * The text on a logo might be truncated.

You can read more about how to manage these in the Action Center Guide.

items.title: Plex & Automation: Why does Posterizarr upload artwork during Tautulli / *Arr runs even if PlexUpload is false?
items.text:
Question: I set PlexUpload: "false" in my configuration because I use Kometa to manage asset uploads and overlays. However, when new media is imported via Tautulli or Radarr/Sonarr triggers, Posterizarr still uploads the poster/background directly to Plex. Is this intended?

Answer: Yes, this is completely intentional by design.

Here is why: * PlexUpload: "false" is designed specifically for scheduled, batch, and normal library runs. In this workflow, Posterizarr generates and stores stylized assets in your /assets directory. Kometa then runs subsequently on a schedule, applies its own overlays/metadata, and pushes the final combined artwork to Plex. * Auto-triggers (Tautulli and Radarr/Sonarr webhooks) are designed for instant real-time fulfillment. When a new movie, show, or episode is added, the trigger's sole purpose is to immediately supply custom Posterizarr artwork to your media server so the new media has a clean, styled poster immediately. If uploads were disabled in trigger mode, the trigger would have no visible effect in Plex until a subsequent Kometa cycle ran (which might be hours or days away).

items.title: Recommended Workflows
items.text:
1. If you want immediate artwork upon media addition (Recommended): Leave Tautulli or *Arr triggers enabled. Newly added media receives styled Posterizarr artwork right away, and whenever Kometa runs later, Kometa will add its overlay flags on top.
  2. If you want ONLY Kometa to ever touch Plex artwork: **Disable Tautulli and Arr triggers entirely*. Instead, schedule Posterizarr to run periodically (e.g., daily at 02:00) before your scheduled Kometa run (e.g., daily at 03:00). With PlexUpload: "false", Posterizarr will generate images exclusively into the /assets directory, and Kometa will perform 100% of the uploads to Plex.

items.title: Plex: How does Collection Diff & Push work in Collection Explorer?
items.text:
Question: How does the Collection Explorer compare local collection posters with Plex, and will it push artwork if I use Kometa?

Answer: Under /media-server-collections, Posterizarr inspects your local Assets/Collections/ directory alongside your Plex collections. It computes a status tag for each collection: * In Sync: The local collection image exists and matches the recorded upload state. * Update Ready: The local image was modified or redesigned and differs from the last uploaded version. * Missing on Plex: A local collection poster exists on disk, but has not yet been pushed to your Plex server. * No Local Asset: A collection exists on Plex, but no matching artwork exists in Assets/Collections/.

You can preview the local image vs. the server image directly using the LOCAL / SERVER switcher on each card. Clicking "Push to Plex" or "Push All Out-of-Sync" performs a direct REST upload (/library/metadata/{rating_key}/posters) and updates the internal cache (database/plex_push_cache.db). This is completely manual and opt-in, so your Kometa configurations remain fully respected unless you explicitly push.

items.title: Plex: Can I schedule automated artwork pushes for only specific asset types?
items.text:
Question: I want Posterizarr to automatically push only my custom Collection posters to Plex on a schedule, while letting Kometa manage movie and TV show posters. Is that possible?

Answer: Yes! In the WebUI under Scheduler (/scheduler), you can create a job with the execution mode set to Plex Sync (Lightweight). When setting up the schedule: 1. Select the library (or All Libraries). 2. In the Asset Types selector, check only Collections (and uncheck Posters, Seasons, Title Cards, Backgrounds). 3. Set your cron schedule or interval (e.g., daily).

This job runs as a fast Python task without invoking PowerShell or ImageMagick, inspects local files for changes against database/plex_push_cache.db, and pushes only your selected asset types to Plex.

Warning for Kometa Users

Never schedule Plex Sync for asset types (like movie/show posters or seasons) that are also managed by Kometa. Because Kometa applies its own overlays directly to Plex, Posterizarr will detect that the server image differs from the local file and will repeatedly attempt to re-upload it, leading to a continuous overwrite war. If you use Kometa, only sync asset types (such as custom Collections) that Kometa does not touch.

items.title: Frontend Components Architecture & Documentation
items.text: This document provides a technical overview of the React frontend architecture and components within Posterizarr's WebUI. The frontend is built using React (Vite) and styled with Tailwind CSS.

items.title: Architecture Overview
items.text: The frontend follows a component-based architecture located entirely within webui/frontend/src/. It is structured to handle configuration management, live monitoring, media galleries, and triggering backend jobs.

items.title: Directory Structure
items.text:
• components/: Reusable React components that make up the UI (pages, modals, forms, galleries).
  • context/: React Context providers for global state management (Theme, Auth, Sidebar, Toast notifications).
  • locales/: Internationalization (i18n) translation files.
  • utils/: Helper functions for API fetching, date formatting, and logging.

items.title: Layout & Navigation
items.text:
• Responsive views: route layouts support narrow phones, tablets, and desktop screens. Action Center bulk/item controls wrap, Scheduler controls stack when needed, Logs filters stay stacked beside a tablet sidebar, and configuration token rows, setting keys, and library labels can shrink or wrap without hiding actions. Mobile form text uses a readable 16px size to avoid focus zoom in mobile browsers.
  • Mobile navigation: the drawer has a viewport-bounded width, its own scroll region, background scroll locking, Escape dismissal, and automatic closing after navigation or switching to desktop width. Theme choices scroll on short screens. Notifications fit the phone width below the navigation bar.
  • Dialog sizing: centered dialogs use app-dialog-backdrop on the fixed overlay and app-dialog-panel on its panel. Shared phone rules bound panels to the dynamic viewport and safe-area insets, allow vertical scrolling, keep header/footer sections from shrinking, and size footer actions for touch. Preserve min-w-0 on shrinking flex/grid children and use local horizontal scrolling for wide tables or code. The shared contract currently covers 54 panels; desktop dimensions remain component-owned.
  • Artwork and setup dialogs: image preview stacks artwork and details below desktop width; Action Center keeps compact, keyboard-accessible preview thumbnails visible on phones. Provider search wraps its title, filters, and search controls. Onboarding keeps the language selector separate from its mobile stepper and its footer outside the scrollable form.

  • Responsive verification: all 37 registered routes (including redirects) were audited at 320px, 768px, and 1440px; all nine configuration tabs were also checked with populated example settings and expanded groups. Interactive checks covered mobile navigation and representative add-library, YAML, variable-editor, sync, ratings-cache, image-preview fallback, and first-run dialogs, including 740x360 landscape. Tests used a local build with read-only API fixtures and blocked live writes. Conditional dialog content, real artwork delivery, device keyboards, and physical iOS/Android behavior still need release QA; shared bounds alone are not a claim that every possible dialog state was exercised.

  • App.jsx: The root component. Handles routing (React Router) and wraps the application in Context providers.

  • View loading: Dashboard and navigation stay eager. Other route views and onboarding use React.lazy with a Suspense loading state; routed content reuses ErrorBoundary for recovery without removing navigation. Blueprints remains shared/eager because replacement-modal controls import it. Build chunks are split by actual route imports instead of manually grouping page modules with Dashboard.
  • Sidebar.jsx: The main side navigation menu.
  • TopNavbar.jsx: The top bar, housing breadcrumbs, user profile, and version badges. Main Posterizarr runs (including scheduled and recently-added triggers) and independent background jobs appear together, each with its own stop action where supported. Multiple jobs use compact, localized labels and icon stop buttons; the task strip scrolls horizontally when needed without covering the language, theme, or user controls. Ratings Refresh links directly to its live log. The existing top bar remains desktop/tablet-only.
  • Dashboard.jsx: The primary landing page. Aggregates statistics, recent assets, and quick-action buttons.

items.title: Configuration & Settings
items.text:
• ConfigEditor.jsx: A dynamic form component for editing the config.json. It fetches tooltips from the backend and handles schema validation.
  • OnboardingModal.jsx: The comprehensive first-run setup wizard that guides users through configuring media servers, schedules, libraries, and notifications.
  • RunModes.jsx: Interface for selecting and triggering the various Posterizarr PowerShell modes (Normal, Backup, Sync, etc.).
  • SchedulerSettings.jsx: UI for managing cron jobs and automated schedules, supporting standard PowerShell execution modes as well as lightweight Python-based Plex Sync jobs with granular library selection and asset type toggles (collections, posters, seasons, title cards, backgrounds).
  • Blueprints.jsx: Interface for managing layout blueprints and recipes.
  • LanguageOrderSelector.jsx & LanguageSwitcher.jsx: Components to handle UI language switching and the priority order of downloaded asset languages.
  • ProviderOrderSelector.jsx: Drag-and-drop interface allowing users to configure the precise fallback order for metadata providers (TMDB, TVDB, Fanart, Plex).
  • LibraryExclusionSelector.jsx: An inline and modal selector used during onboarding and configuration to include or exclude specific libraries from being processed.

items.title: Media & Assets Management
items.text:
• AssetsManager.jsx & AssetOverview.jsx: High-level views for managing generated posters, local assets, and storage usage.
  • Action Center paging: AssetOverview requests /api/assets/overview/page with page size, tab, status, category, search, type, and library. Search is debounced; obsolete requests are aborted and ignored. Only visible rows are transferred during browsing, while counts and filter options describe the full result set. Filter controls remain mounted during refresh, selections retain their records across pages, and confirmed all-filtered bulk actions explicitly fetch all matching records before submitting changes.
  • RecentAssets.jsx: Dashboard carousel displaying recently processed assets with direct integration into AssetReplacer for instant correction.
  • GalleryHub.jsx, Gallery.jsx, SeasonGallery.jsx, TitleCardGallery.jsx, TestGallery.jsx: Interactive grids displaying generated artwork with lazy loading, filtering, pagination, and detailed inspection.
  • BackgroundsGallery.jsx: Specialized gallery for viewing and selecting background source images.
  • ManualAssets.jsx & FolderView.jsx: Tree and grid explorer for user-provided images under /manualassets that override automated scrapers.
  • BackupAssets.jsx: Gallery view for inspecting and managing original images preserved under /assetsbackup.
  • ImagePreviewModal.jsx: A modal component to view full-resolution posters, EXIF metadata, and provider links.
  • AssetReplacer.jsx: Deep inspection and replacement modal for swapping out posters or logos on the fly.
  • Replacement metadata: when metadata is not supplied, export and image-choice requests include rootfolder instead of downloading complete libraries. Existing library and exact episode matching are preserved, and closing or switching the asset aborts obsolete metadata requests.
  • AssetSearchModal.jsx: Provider search modal (TMDB, TVDB, Fanart) to find and apply replacement artwork or clearlogos by title or ID.
  • LogoBrowser.jsx: Media server library browser for inspecting, filtering, and uploading missing ClearLogos directly to Plex, Jellyfin, or Emby.
  • CollectionExplorer.jsx: Visual collection manager listing collections across connected media servers. Displays enriched collection metadata (item count and release year ranges, e.g. 12 items • 1979 - 2024), Asset Details modal inspection (ImagePreviewModal.jsx), real-time diff status badges (In Sync, Update Ready, Missing on Plex, No Local Asset), quick diff view toggling (LOCAL vs SERVER), 1-click single-poster push to Plex, batch out-of-sync push, and status filtering.
  • CollectionLiveEditor.jsx: Real-time interactive collection poster designer featuring linear/radial gradients, top/bottom matte fades, vignettes, tiled grain, border radius, typography alignment/drop shadows, preset thumbnails, and direct media server uploads.

items.title: Monitoring & Status
items.text:
• DynamicOverlays.jsx: Sync & Maintenance has separate URL-addressable views for synchronization, media changes, episode title review, overlay cache, and ratings cache. Only the active view is rendered; shared settings, sync state, dialogs, and background jobs remain intact. Navigation supports keyboard arrows/Home/End, saved view selection, and legacy tab=cache links.
  • EpisodeTitleReview.jsx: Historical ImageChoices title comparison with existing-artwork previews, eligibility reasons, filtered paging, and confirmed single/selected/all recreation. Recreation uses the existing asset queue rather than a separate renderer.
  • LogViewer.jsx: A real-time terminal-like component that connects to the backend WebSocket to stream Posterizarr execution logs.
  • QueueView.jsx: Displays backend task queue states (running, pending, completed, failed) with abort controls.
  • RuntimeStats.jsx & RuntimeHistory.jsx: Charts and tables displaying historical execution metrics, processing durations, and asset counts.
  • SystemInfo.jsx: Displays host system resources (CPU, Memory, Alpine/Docker environment, versions).
  • AssetsStats.jsx: Real-time counter widgets for library folders, poster counts, and total asset sizes.

items.title: Integrations & Export
items.text:
• PlexExport.jsx & JellyfinEmbyExport.jsx: Interfaces dedicated to managing metadata and artwork sync for specific media servers.
  • AutoTriggers.jsx: UI to configure automated webhooks from Radarr, Sonarr, or Tautulli.
  • PlexOAuthButton.jsx: Interactive OAuth component allowing users to log into Plex and automatically retrieve their server token.

items.title: Utility, Feedback & Modal Components
items.text:
• Auto-Queue Changes: a standard checkbox appears directly below Add to Queue, only while queueing is on, in both Manual Mode and asset replacement dialogs. The shared preference persists as auto_queue_changes in WebUI settings (default false). In Manual Mode, it keeps queueing selected after successful URL or upload submissions; the user still submits the completed form explicitly. In replacement dialogs, choosing provider artwork or selecting a ratio-validated upload submits it to the existing asset queue without a second replacement confirmation. The per-item queue switch stays on while this preference is active. Browsing, invalid uploads, and text-field edits alone do not submit anything. Existing parameter validation still applies, failed attempts remain available for manual retry, and duplicate in-flight replacement submissions are blocked. Queued success is reported as queued, not as an already completed replacement; parent completion callbacks are not invoked before processing, so Action Center entries are not removed just because work was queued. Logo selection retains its separate workflow.
  • ConfirmDialog.jsx & ToastNotification.jsx: Reusable components for user feedback and destructive action confirmation.
  • DangerZone.jsx: A section component for high-risk actions (factory reset, wipe database).
  • RestoreModeModal.jsx: Targeted restore modal allowing users to restore artwork filtered by library, item title/folder, and asset type.
  • ValidateButton.jsx: Triggers backend configuration validation (CheckJson) with status feedback.
  • VersionBadge.jsx & ReleasesSection.jsx: Visual version indicators and GitHub release notes viewer.
  • ImageSizeSlider.jsx & CompactImageSizeSlider.jsx: UI controls for adjusting the size of items in gallery grids.
  • ScrollToButtons.jsx: Floating helper to quickly navigate to the top or bottom of extensive media libraries.

items.title: Global State (src/context/)
items.text:
• AuthContext.jsx: Manages user authentication tokens, basic auth states, and session persistence.
  • ThemeContext.jsx: Toggles between light, dark, and system color palettes using Tailwind CSS variables.
  • ToastContext.jsx: Exposes a hook (useToast) to fire non-blocking notification alerts throughout the UI.
  • SidebarContext.jsx: Manages responsive expansion/collapse states for the navigation sidebar.
  • DashboardLoadingContext.jsx: Coordinates startup loading transitions, dashboard data prefetching, and splash screens.

items.title: Contribution Guidelines
items.text:
When making a Pull Request to the React frontend:

  • Styling: Always use Tailwind CSS utility classes. Avoid creating custom CSS in index.css unless absolutely necessary.
  • API Calls: Use the pre-configured wrappers in src/utils/fetchInterceptor.js for API requests to ensure Auth headers and error handling are uniformly applied.
  • New Pages: If you create a new page component, be sure to add the route in App.jsx and the navigation link in Sidebar.jsx.
  • Localization: Do not hardcode user-facing strings. Use the useTranslation hook and add keys to the JSON files in src/locales/.

items.title: First-time setup
items.text:
This guide is for someone opening Posterizarr for the first time. Follow it in order; you do not need to understand every setting before getting started.

After opening the Web UI, start at Dashboard in the left sidebar. The sidebar remains the main route to configuration, runs, assets, builders, and automation.

items.title: 1. Choose how to install
items.text:
• Docker: the recommended route for most home servers. Start with Choose an installation method.
  • Unraid: install the Community Apps version, then check the Unraid notes.
  • Windows or Linux without Docker: use the manual PowerShell walkthrough.

The separate Web UI from source guide is for development or manual UI setups, not the normal Docker or Unraid installation.

items.title: 2. Gather only what you plan to use
items.text:
Have your media-server address and API credentials ready. Add artwork-provider credentials for the providers you want to search. Start with the requirements checklist; optional services can be configured later.

Open Configuration > Providers to enter only the artwork-provider keys you plan to use.

Keep API keys private. Do not paste them into screenshots, support posts, or public configuration files.

items.title: 3. Start Posterizarr and open the Web UI
items.text:
After installation, open the Web UI from the same machine or network as the server. Docker's default published port is 8000, so the local address is usually http://localhost:8000; replace localhost with the server address when opening it from another device. If it is not reachable, see Networking.

If the first-run setup appears, use it to connect your media server and choose the libraries Posterizarr should manage. Otherwise, open the configuration area in the Web UI and check the same items there. Do not enable every library just to get through setup; begin with one test library.

items.title: Automatic First-Run Wizard
items.text:
The wizard appears automatically while the initial configuration is incomplete. Choose a primary server, validate its connection, and select libraries before continuing.

The wizard is a nine-step modal, not a sidebar page. It opens automatically when Posterizarr has not recorded setup as complete. Finish Setup saves its configuration; before then, form edits remain in the wizard. Continue is gated on a validated server/library selection and on entering all three provider keys.

Step What it configures Welcome Introduces the guided setup. Media Server Choose Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, or experimental Silo; enter credentials, test the connection, and select libraries. Plex users can optionally configure a secondary Jellyfin or Emby sync. API Keys Enter a TMDb Read Access Token, TheTVDB Project API key, and Fanart.tv personal key. These three fields are required to continue in this wizard; the Test buttons are available for each provider. Automation Choose whether to clean unused assets, skip Japanese/Chinese titles, and skip TBA title cards. Leave cleanup off until library scope and exclusions are correct. Performance Set Image Processing, output quality, retained logs, and parallel jobs. Lower parallel jobs on memory-limited NAS devices. Notifications Choose none, Discord, or Apprise; Uptime Kuma can be configured separately. Dynamic Overlays Optional. Enable the feature and continue into its dedicated Setup Wizard after finishing. It starts in Dry Run. Schedule Optional. Choose a run mode and daily, weekly, monthly, or interval schedule. Logo Updater also exposes library, force-replace, EXIF-check, and revert options. Ready Save the configuration and complete onboarding. If scheduling was enabled, the wizard enables the scheduler and creates the selected job. If Dynamic Overlays was enabled, its Setup Wizard opens; otherwise the wizard opens How It Works.

Enable Dynamic Overlays here to open its guided setup after finishing. The first-run choice keeps Dry Run on and does not upload artwork.

For Docker, set RUN_TIME=disabled before enabling a schedule here so the container timer does not compete with the Web UI Scheduler. If you leave the schedule switch off, no onboarding schedule is created.

Open Configuration > Media Servers to validate the server URL/key and choose the first library.

items.title: 4. Check what Posterizarr will create
items.text:
There are two different test workflows, both available in the Web UI:

  • Artwork styling: open Run Modes > Testing Mode. It creates sample images using your current settings and opens the results in Test Gallery. It does not upload artwork to a live media server. See Testing Mode.
  • Dynamic Overlays: open Builders > Dynamic Overlays, use its Setup Wizard, select one library, and keep Dry Run enabled while checking rules and previews. Dynamic Overlay Dry Run renders changes but does not upload artwork. See the Dynamic Overlays guide.

These are separate checks: Testing Mode checks generated artwork styling, while Dynamic Overlays Dry Run checks overlay rules and placement.

items.title: 5. Run a small first job
items.text: Start with one library or a targeted item. Before a normal run, review whether direct upload is enabled for your media server and where generated assets will be stored. The configuration reference explains those settings. If you use Dynamic Overlays, keep Dry Run enabled until the preview, library scope, and logs look right.

items.title: 6. Automate only after checking the result
items.text: Once the artwork looks right and the destination is correct, configure a schedule or an integration such as Sonarr, Radarr, or Tautulli. See Run modes and automation. You can return to Posterizarr's main features, browse the artwork showcase, or open the guide for a specific task from Use Posterizarr in the navigation.

items.title: Homepage Custom API Integration
items.text: You can integrate Posterizarr statistics into your Homepage dashboard using the customapi widget type. This allows you to display global stats or specific library stats directly on your dashboard.

items.title: Identifying Library Indices
items.text:
To map specific libraries or collections in the examples below, you need to know their index in the folders array returned by the API.

  1. Open your browser and navigate to: http://your-ip:8003/api/assets/stats?api_key=your_api_key
  2. You will see a JSON response like this:
{
  "success": true,
  "stats": {
    "folders": [
      { "name": "Anime Shows", ... }, // Index [0]
      { "name": "TV Shows", ... },    // Index [1]
      { "name": "Kids Shows", ... },  // Index [2]
      ...
    ]
  }
}
  1. Count the folders starting from 0. For example:
    • The first folder is stats.folders[0]
    • The second folder is stats.folders[1]
    • ... and so on.

items.title: Live Status & Global Asset Statistics (Recommended)
items.text:
This configuration combines Docker health monitoring with dual customapi widgets to provide a comprehensive, real-time service card: - Docker Status: Displays live container status (e.g. RUNNING) in the card header. - Asset Statistics (/api/assets/stats): Shows real-time counts for Posters, Seasons, Titlecards, and total asset disk Size. - Scheduler & Run Monitor (/api/dashboard/all): Shows the current active mode (Running) and the relative countdown to the next scheduled run (Next Run).

Active Run (During Execution)Idle (Between Runs) 

- Posterizarr:
    icon: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fscorrupt/posterizarr/main/docs/images/Logo_Posterizarr.png
    href: https://posterizarr.your-domain.com # or http://your-ip:8003
    server: my-docker # Optional: matches your docker provider in Homepage's docker.yaml
    container: posterizarr # Optional: docker container name for live status badge
    widgets:
      - type: customapi
        url: http://your-ip:8003/api/assets/stats?api_key=your_api_key
        display: block
        mappings:
          - field: stats.posters
            label: Posters
          - field: stats.seasons
            label: Seasons
          - field: stats.titlecards
            label: Titlecards
          - field: stats.total_size
            label: Size
            format: bytes
      - type: customapi
        url: http://your-ip:8003/api/dashboard/all?api_key=your_api_key
        display: block
        mappings:
          - field: status.current_mode
            label: Running
          - field: scheduler_status.next_run
            label: Next Run
            format: date
            timeStyle: short
            locale: de-DE # Optional: adjust to your locale (e.g. en-US, de-DE) or use format: relativeDate

items.title: Overall Assets & Stats
items.text:
This example shows how to combine both the overview (for missing assets) and stats (for counts) endpoints in a single service block using YAML anchors for a cleaner configuration.

Index may differ

This example uses stats.folders[8] for Collections. Please look at Identifying Library Indices to find the correct index for your system.

- Posterizarr:
    - Assets:
        icon: https://github.com/fscorrupt/posterizarr/blob/main/docs/images/Logo_Posterizarr.png?raw=true
        widgets:
          - type: customapi
            url: http://your-ip:8003/api/assets/overview?api_key=your_api_key
            display: block
            mappings:
              - field: categories.missing_assets.count
                label: Missing

          - &stats_api
            type: customapi
            url: http://your-ip:8003/api/assets/stats?api_key=your_api_key
            display: block
            mappings:
              - field: stats.posters
                label: Posters
              - field: stats.folders[8].poster_count
                label: Collections
              - field: stats.seasons
                label: Seasons

          - <<: *stats_api
            display: block
            mappings:
              - field: stats.backgrounds
                label: Backgrounds
              - field: stats.titlecards
                label: Titlecards
              - field: stats.total_size
                label: Size
                format: bytes

items.title: Global Statistics
items.text:
To display overall statistics (Total Posters, Seasons, etc.), use the following configuration in your services.yaml:

- Posterizarr Assets:
    icon: https://github.com/fscorrupt/posterizarr/blob/main/docs/images/Logo_Posterizarr.png?raw=true
    widget:
      type: customapi
      url: http://your-ip:8003/api/assets/stats?api_key=your_api_key
      display: list
      mappings:
        - field: stats.posters
          label: Total Posters
        - field: stats.backgrounds
          label: Total Backgrounds
        - field: stats.seasons
          label: Total Seasons
        - field: stats.titlecards
          label: Total Titlecards
        - field: stats.folders[8].poster_count
          label: Total Collections
        - field: stats.total_size
          label: Total Size
          format: bytes

items.title: Docker Labels Configuration
items.text:
If you prefer to configure Homepage automatically via Docker labels instead of manually editing services.yaml, you can add the following labels to your Posterizarr container:

      - homepage.name=Posterizarr
      - homepage.icon=sh-posterizarr
      - homepage.href=${POSTERIZARR_URL}
      - homepage.siteMonitor=${POSTERIZARR_URL}
      - homepage.widget.type=customapi
      - homepage.widget.url=${POSTERIZARR_URL}/api/assets/stats?api_key=${POSTERIZARR_KEY}
      - homepage.widget.display=block
      - homepage.widget.mappings[0].field=stats.posters
      - homepage.widget.mappings[0].label=Posters
      - homepage.widget.mappings[1].field=stats.seasons
      - homepage.widget.mappings[1].label=Seasons
      - homepage.widget.mappings[2].field=stats.titlecards
      - homepage.widget.mappings[2].label=Titlecards
      - homepage.widget.mappings[3].field=stats.total_size
      - homepage.widget.mappings[3].label=Size
      - homepage.widget.mappings[3].format=bytes

items.title: Library-Specific Statistics
items.text: You can also create separate widgets for each of your libraries (Anime, TV Shows, Movies, etc.).

items.title: Example: Library Widgets
items.text:
Here is an example configuration for multiple libraries using YAML anchors for efficiency:

- Posterizarr:
    - Anime Shows:
        widget: &lib_base  # <--- This defines the "lib_base" anchor
          type: customapi
          url: http://your-ip:8003/api/assets/stats?api_key=your_api_key
          mappings:
            - field: stats.folders[0].poster_count
              label: Posters
            - field: stats.folders[0].season_count
              label: Seasons
            - field: stats.folders[0].titlecard_count
              label: Titlecards
            - field: stats.folders[0].size
              label: Size
              format: bytes

    - TV Shows:
        widget:
          <<: *lib_base
          mappings:
            - field: stats.folders[1].poster_count # Only override the field index
              label: Posters
            - field: stats.folders[1].season_count
              label: Seasons
            - field: stats.folders[1].titlecard_count
              label: Titlecards
            - field: stats.folders[1].size
              label: Size
              format: bytes

    - Movies:
        widget:
          <<: *lib_base
          mappings:
            - field: stats.folders[3].poster_count
              label: Posters
            - field: stats.folders[3].size
              label: Size
              format: bytes

    - 4K TV Shows:
        widget:
          <<: *lib_base
          mappings:
            - field: stats.folders[5].poster_count
              label: Posters
            - field: stats.folders[5].season_count
              label: Seasons
            - field: stats.folders[5].titlecard_count
              label: Titlecards
            - field: stats.folders[5].size
              label: Size
              format: bytes

items.title: Example: Collections Widget
items.text:
Since the index for Collections varies between systems, you must first identify it using the guide above. If your Collections are at index [8], your configuration would look like this:

- Posterizarr:
    - Collections:
        widget:
          type: customapi
          url: http://your-ip:8003/api/assets/stats?api_key=your_api_key
          mappings:
            - field: stats.folders[8].poster_count
              label: Collection Posters
            - field: stats.folders[8].size
              label: Size
              format: bytes

items.title: Custom CSS Styling (Dark Glassmorphism)

/* ==============================================================================
