  • MaxWidth (str), MaxHeight (str), text_offset (str), lineSpacing (str), TextGravity (str): Bounding box layout.

items.title: 10. SeasonPosterOverlayPart (Season Posters)
items.text:
• Same typography, border, and overlay controls as PosterOverlayPart.
  • ShowFallback (bool): Fall back to show poster if season artwork is missing.
  • OverrideSeasonName (bool): Override default season text.
  • SeasonOverrideText (str): Custom regular season title (e.g. "Staffel").
  • SpecialSeasonOverrideText (str): Custom specials season title (e.g. "Spezial").

items.title: 11. ShowTitleOnSeasonPosterPart
items.text:
• AddShowTitletoSeason (bool): Add series title or logo above the season text.
  • Standard typography, stroke, point size, and layout settings.

items.title: 12. CollectionTitlePosterPart
items.text:
• AddCollectionTitle (bool): Add a secondary "Collection" badge or text.
  • CollectionTitle (str): Label string (default: "Collection").

items.title: 13. CollectionPosterOverlayPart
items.text: • Typography, borders, overlays, and bounding box parameters for collection posters.

items.title: 14. BackgroundOverlayPart
items.text: • Compositing, typography, and border settings for 3840x2160 backgrounds.

items.title: 15. TitleCardOverlayPart
items.text:
• UseBackgroundAsTitleCard (bool): Use show background image as base for episode title card.
  • BackgroundFallback (bool): Fall back to background if episode thumb is missing.
  • AddOverlay (bool), AddBorder (bool), bordercolor (str), borderwidth (str).
  • SkipWords (array): Keywords or regex expressions that trigger title card skipping.

items.title: 16. TitleCardTitleTextPart
items.text: • Episode title typography, point sizes (minPointSize: 50, maxPointSize: 150), and bounding box.

items.title: 17. TitleCardEPTextPart
items.text:
• Season and episode index labeling (e.g. SeasonTCText: "Season", EpisodeTCText: "Episode").
  • Formats text as SEASON 1 • EPISODE 5.

items.title: 13. Critical Rules, Gotchas & Conventions for AI Agents
items.text:
1. Schema Synchronization (CheckJson):
  2. Every new configuration property introduced in the codebase MUST be added to config.example.json.
  3. If a key is missing from config.example.json, CheckJson will flag it as obsolete and silently delete it from user configurations during container startup!

  4. Ensure branch detection ($env:APP_VERSION -match 'dev') points to the dev branch template when editing development branches.

  5. Provider Resolution & Linking (FavProviderLink):

  6. In AssetOverview.jsx and AssetReplacer.jsx, FavProviderLink provides a direct link to the user's preferred upstream provider so missing metadata can be reported or fixed.

  7. Even if an asset was acquired from a secondary fallback provider, PrimaryProvider represents the intended preferred provider.

  8. PowerShell Argument Escaping & Command Construction:

  9. In CoreGeneration.ps1, arguments passed to magick must be constructed as discrete PowerShell string arrays rather than single interpolated strings.

  10. Take extreme care with path separators and nested quotation between Windows (\) and Linux (/).

  11. Multi-Threaded Log Parsing ([Txx] Worker IDs):

  12. When parallel jobs run (ParallelJobs > 1), log entries in Scriptlog.log from different threads are interleaved.

  13. Always group and trace log messages by their Runspace Worker ID (e.g., [T14]) to reconstruct the sequential execution of a single media item.

  14. SSRF & Path Traversal Security:

  15. All backend image proxying, clearlogo fetching, and webhook callbacks must pass through is_safe_url to prevent SSRF against loopback or unauthorized private network endpoints.

  16. User-supplied file paths must always be validated via get_safe_path against base_dir.

  17. WebUI Configuration Normalization:

  18. The backend supports both grouped structures (config["ApiPart"]["FavProvider"]) and flat representations (config["FavProvider"]).

  19. Use config_mapper.py or existing helper methods when querying or saving configuration via /api/config.

  20. No Dummy Placeholders:

  21. Never commit empty or dummy mock files for image processing. Posterizarr relies on actual ImageMagick or Pillow pipelines to generate valid binary artwork.

items.title: Run Modes and Automation
items.text:
Posterizarr is designed to be operated from the Web UI. You do not need a terminal or PowerShell for the normal artwork workflow. Open Run Modes from the left sidebar to run, test, back up, restore, sync, or create one asset.

Choose Run Modes in the left sidebar. Quick Run cards start common jobs; the manual form below creates or replaces one asset.

items.title: Quick Run modes
items.text: Quick Run cards are at the top of Run Modes. If a confirmation dialog opens, review it before starting. You can choose Don't show this again in supported dialogs; use Reset Prompts at the top of Quick Run to show them again. Only one script run can be active at a time. While one is running, its status and a Stop button appear on the page.

items.title: Normal Mode
items.text: Choose Normal Mode to process the libraries and artwork types selected in your configuration. Review the confirmation dialog, especially the target server, enabled libraries, upload behavior, and asset cleanup settings, then start the run. Use Testing Mode first if you have changed styling or blueprints and want sample output before a library run.

items.title: Testing Mode
items.text:
1. In Run Modes > Quick Run, choose Testing Mode.
  2. Confirm that the dialog says no artwork will be uploaded to Plex, Jellyfin, or Emby. The generated examples use your current asset styling and settings.
  3. Choose Start Test Run, or Start & Go to Gallery to open the results automatically when generation finishes.
  4. Review the samples in Test Gallery in the sidebar. The confirmation dialog also lets you set automatic redirection for future test runs.

Testing Mode is for checking generated artwork. It is separate from Dynamic Overlays > Dry Run, which tests overlay rules and renders their changes without uploading them.

The examples below are current Testing Mode outputs from the supplied test set. They show how short, medium, long, and uppercase text affect each artwork type. Open the full Artwork Showcase for additional formats and real media-server examples.

Poster · Short text Show poster · Long, uppercase Season poster · Medium text Background · Short, uppercase Show background · Medium text Titlecard · Long, uppercase

items.title: Backup Mode
items.text: Choose Backup Mode to copy existing media-server artwork into the configured backup location. Confirm the destination and start the backup. This preserves a local copy for recovery; it does not generate new artwork.

items.title: Restore Mode
items.text: Choose Restore Mode to upload artwork from the local backup folder back to your media server. In the dialog, choose Restore All Libraries or Restore Specific Items. The specific-item filters can narrow by library, folder/item name, and asset type. Restoring all libraries can affect a large part of your server, so select a narrow target when you only need one item. Restored images are uploaded as saved; this step does not run them through the current overlay or artwork styling configuration.

items.title: Sync Jellyfin, Emby, or Silo
items.text: Use the Jellyfin or Emby sync card to copy artwork from Plex to the selected server. Review the confirmation details first. Library names must match exactly between the source and target servers. Silo has its own Sync Silo action and limitations; see the Silo notes.

items.title: Logo Updater
items.text: Choose Logo Updater to fetch or manage logos for one library or all suitable libraries. The dialog offers Browse for a single library, Process All Libraries, Only Replace Non-Posterizarr Logos (EXIF Check), Force Replace, and Revert. Force Replace may overwrite existing logos; Revert removes logos previously added by Posterizarr. Review those switches before starting.

items.title: Reset Posters
items.text: Enter the exact library name in the Reset Posters section and choose Reset. Posterizarr asks for confirmation before replacing selected posters with the media server's available default artwork. This changes live server artwork and cannot be undone by Posterizarr; make a backup first if you may want to restore the current images.

items.title: Create one asset manually
items.text:
Use the Manual form below the Quick Run cards when you want to make or replace one item without processing a full library:

  1. Choose the output type: poster, season poster, titlecard, background, or collection poster. For standard posters and backgrounds, also choose movie or TV show.
  2. Search by title and year in the built-in provider search, then select an image. Or upload your own image or provide an image URL/path.
  3. Choose the library and item. Use Select Library and Select Folder to browse what the connected server exposes.
  4. Fill in the type-specific details. Season posters need a season name; titlecards need a season, episode title, and episode number.
  5. Select a blueprint or keep the global configuration. Review text/textless and title/logo options, then choose Run or Add to Queue.

The Auto-Queue Changes checkbox remembers the queue choice for future manual submissions. It is separate from the queue switch for the current asset.

items.title: Schedule and automate
items.text:
• Use Scheduler in the sidebar to create, edit, enable, or run scheduled jobs. Choose the mode, libraries, asset types where available, and schedule.
  • Use Auto Triggers to connect supported Tautulli or Sonarr/Radarr events. The native webhook setup does not require a terminal or a custom script.
  • Use Logs to review a run. Return to Run Modes to stop an active run.

items.title: Native webhook setup
items.text:
Tautulli: In Tautulli, open Settings > Notification Agents, add a Webhook, and enter http://YOUR_POSTERIZARR_HOST:8000/api/webhook/tautulli?api_key=YOUR_API_KEY. Set the method to POST, enable Recently Added, and provide the JSON data for rating key and media type. Create the API key in Posterizarr's Web UI configuration.

Sonarr or Radarr: Open Settings > Connect, add a Webhook, and enter http://YOUR_POSTERIZARR_HOST:8000/api/webhook/arr?api_key=YOUR_API_KEY. Enable On Import and On Upgrade, set the method to POST, then save. No script file or shared container volume is needed for the native webhook.

See the Tautulli and Sonarr/Radarr setup notes for the external-app steps.

items.title: CLI and legacy instructions (optional)
items.text:
The commands below are not required when using the Web UI. Expand this section only if you intentionally run Posterizarr from PowerShell, Docker exec, or an older script-based trigger integration.

Optional PowerShell, Docker, and legacy trigger commands

items.title: Automatic Mode
items.text:
Run the script without any parameters:

.\Posterizarr.ps1

On docker this way:

  docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1

This will generate posters for your entire Plex library based on the configured settings.

The posters are all placed in AssetPath\.... This can then be mounted in Kometa to use as the assets folder.

items.title: Testing Mode
items.text:
Run the script with the -Testing flag. In this mode, the script will create pink posters/backgrounds with short, medium, and long texts (also in CAPS), using the values specified in the config.json file.

These test images are placed in the script root under the ./test folder.

Tip

This is handy for testing your configuration before applying it en masse to the actual posters. You can see how and where the text would be applied, as well as the size of the textbox.

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -Testing

On docker this way:

docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Testing

items.title: Manual Mode (Interactive)
items.text:
Warning

Source picture gets edited by script and is then moved to desired asset location.

Run the script with the -Manual switch and add the desired extra switch for which poster you want to create -MoviePosterCard or -ShowPosterCard or-SeasonPoster or -CollectionCard or -BackgroundCard or -TitleCard

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual -MoviePosterCard

On docker this way:

docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual -MoviePosterCard

Follow the prompts to enter the source picture path (Container needs Access to it), media folder name, and movie/show title to manually create a custom poster.

Posterizarr Input Prompts

Enter local path or URL to source picture:

  • Paste the image URL or provide the full local path to the image file you want to use as the poster source. This is the image that Posterizarr will base the new poster on.

Enter Media Folder Name (as seen by Plex):

  • The name of the local movie or show folder where the .mkv (or other media) file is stored. This should match the folder structure Plex recognizes.

Enter Movie/Show/Collection Title:

  • The title that will be displayed on the generated poster.

Create Season Poster? (y/n):

  • Type y if you're generating a season poster, otherwise n.

Create TitleCard? (y/n):

  • Type y if you also want to create a title card, otherwise n.

Create Collection Poster? (y/n):

  • Type y if you're generating a collection poster, otherwise n.

Enter Plex Library Name:

  • Enter the name of the Plex (or Jellyfin) library, e.g., "Movies" or "TV Shows".

Enter Title Text:

  • Enter the Title of the asset e.g., "Avatar".

Enter Season Name:

  • Enter the Title of the asset e.g., "Season 1".
  • If you want to add Custom Text to Season poster please enter it via prefix Title | Season 1

items.title: Manual Mode (Semi Automated)
items.text:
Warning

The source picture is moved (if local) or downloaded (if a URL - and moved), then edited and placed in the desired asset location. The -PicturePath parameter can accept either a local file path or a direct URL to an image.

Example on Windows:
  -PicturePath "C:\path\to\movie_bg.jpg"

Example on Docker:
  -PicturePath "/path/to/movie_bg.jpg"

Example with URL:
  -PicturePath "https://posterurl.here/movie_bg.jpg"

Movie or Show Poster

To create a standard poster for a movie or a TV show's main entry:

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual -PicturePath "C:\path\to\movie_bg.jpg" -Titletext "The Martian" -FolderName "The Martian (2015)" -LibraryName "Movies"

On docker this way:

docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual -PicturePath "/path/to/movie_bg.jpg" -Titletext "The Martian" -FolderName "The Martian (2015)" -LibraryName "Movies"

Season Poster

Note

Any season name ending in 0 or 00 (e.g., "Season 0", "Staffel 00") or matching a keyword like "Specials" will be handled as a Specials season. If you want to add Custom Text to Season poster please enter it via prefix Title | Season 01 in -SeasonPosterName

To create a poster for a specific season of a TV show, use the -SeasonPoster switch and provide the season name:

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual -SeasonPoster -PicturePath "C:\path\to\show_bg.jpg" -Titletext "The Mandalorian" -FolderName "The Mandalorian (2019)" -LibraryName "TV Shows" -SeasonPosterName "Season 1"

On docker this way:

docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual -SeasonPoster -PicturePath "/path/to/show_bg.jpg" -Titletext "The Mandalorian" -FolderName "The Mandalorian (2019)" -LibraryName "TV Shows" -SeasonPosterName "Season 1"

Collection Poster

To create a poster for a media collection, use the -CollectionCard switch. The script will use the -Titletext for both the poster text and the folder name.

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual -CollectionCard -PicturePath "C:\path\to\collection_bg.jpg" -Titletext "James Bond" -LibraryName "Movies"

On docker this way:

docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual -CollectionCard -PicturePath "/path/to/collection_bg.jpg" -Titletext "James Bond" -LibraryName "Movies"

Background Poster

To create a standard background poster for a movie or a TV show's main entry:

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual -BackgroundCard -PicturePath "C:\path\to\movie_bg.jpg" -Titletext "The Martian" -FolderName "The Martian (2015)" -LibraryName "Movies"

On docker this way:

docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual -BackgroundCard -PicturePath "/path/to/movie_bg.jpg" -Titletext "The Martian" -FolderName "The Martian (2015)" -LibraryName "Movies"

Episode Title Card

To create a 16:9 title card for a specific episode, use the -TitleCard switch and provide episode details:

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual -TitleCard -PicturePath "C:\path\to\episode_bg.jpg" -FolderName "Breaking Bad (2008)" -LibraryName "TV Shows" -EPTitleName "Ozymandias" -SeasonPosterName "Season 5" -EpisodeNumber "14"

On docker this way:

docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual -TitleCard -PicturePath "/path/to/episode_bg.jpg" -FolderName "Breaking Bad (2008)" -LibraryName "TV Shows" -EPTitleName "Ozymandias" -SeasonPosterName "Season 5" -EpisodeNumber "14"

items.title: Backup Mode
items.text:
Run the script with the -Backup flag. In this mode, the script will download every artwork you have in your mediaserver, using the values specified in the config.json file.

Tip

This is handy for creating a backup or if you want an second assetfolder with kometa/tcm EXIF data for jellyfin/emby.

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -Backup

On docker this way:

  docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Backup

items.title: Restore Mode
items.text:
Run the script with the -Restore flag. In this mode, the script will push all artwork from your local backup folder to your media server (Plex, Jellyfin, or Emby).

Tip

This is handy for quickly recreating your library posters after a crash, or if you prefer to edit assets in bulk locally and then push them.

Warning

Running this command directly without any additional flags will automatically attempt to restore ALL assets for ALL items across ALL your included libraries. To prevent this, use the targeted restore flags below.

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -Restore

On docker this way:

  docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Restore

Targeted Restore You can filter what gets restored using additional flags. These flags can be used independently or combined together. For example, you don't need to specify the library or type if you only want to restore one specific item.

  • -RestoreType (options: poster, background, season, episode, titlecard)
  • -RestoreLibrary (e.g. "Movies")
  • -RestoreItem (Accepts the exact Media Title, the Original Title, OR the exact Root Folder name!)

Examples:

Restore only the posters for a specific movie using its exact folder name: 

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -Restore -RestoreItem "Alien (1979) [imdb-tt0078748]" -RestoreType "poster"

Restore all artwork types for a specific show using its title: 

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -Restore -RestoreItem "Breaking Bad"

Restore only backgrounds for an entire library: 

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -Restore -RestoreLibrary "Movies" -RestoreType "background"

items.title: Poster reset Mode
items.text:
Run the script with the -PosterReset -LibraryToReset "Test Lib" flag. In this mode, posterizarr will reset every artwork from a specifc plex lib.

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -PosterReset -LibraryToReset "Test Lib"

On docker this way:

  docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -PosterReset -LibraryToReset "Test Lib"

Tip

Note: This operation does not delete any artwork. It simply sets each item's poster to the first available poster from Plex’s metadata. This action cannot be undone, so proceed with caution.

items.title: Sync Modes
items.text:
Exact Match

The script requires that library names in Plex and Emby/Jellyfin match exactly for the sync to work. It calculates the hash of the artwork from both servers to determine if there are differences, and only syncs the artwork if the hashes do not match.

items.title: Jellyfin
items.text:
Run the script with the -SyncJelly flag. In this mode, the script will sync every artwork you have in plex to jellyfin.

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -SyncJelly

On docker this way:

  docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -SyncJelly

items.title: Emby
items.text:
Run the script with the -SyncEmby flag. In this mode, the script will sync every artwork you have in plex to emby.

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -SyncEmby

On docker this way:

  docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -SyncEmby

Tip

This is handy if you want to run the sync after a kometa run, then you have kometa ovlerayed images in jelly/emby

items.title: Tautulli Mode Docker
items.text:
Warning

Tautulli and Posterizarr must run as a container in Docker

Note

If Discord is configured it will send a Notification on each trigger.

Direct Upload Enforced in Trigger Modes

Tautulli Mode always forces direct upload to Plex (Upload2Plex = true), regardless of whether PlexUpload is set to false in your config.json. The purpose of real-time triggers is to immediately style newly added media in Plex the moment it is imported, without waiting for your next scheduled run. If you use Kometa and want zero uploads from Posterizarr before Kometa applies overlays, do not configure Tautulli triggers; schedule regular Posterizarr batch runs before your Kometa schedule instead.

This mode lets Tautulli trigger Posterizarr for a specific Plex item, such as a newly added show, movie, or episode.

For the legacy script-based setup, configure a script in Tautulli as follows.

  1. Make sure that you mount the Posterizarr directory to tautulli, cause the script needs the Path /posterizarr 
    volumes:
  - "/opt/appdata/posterizarr:/posterizarr:rw"
  # Optional: Add additional mounts if running multiple instances
  # - "/opt/appdata/posterizarr2:/posterizarr2:rw"
    ⚠️ Note: The default mount path is case-sensitive and must match exactly /posterizarr. If you use custom paths for multiple instances, ensure they are also mounted here.
  2. Download the trigger.py from the GH and place it in the Tautulli Script dir - Tautulli-Wiki
  3. You may have to set chmod +x to the file.
  4. Open Tautulli and go to Settings - NOTIFICATION AGENTS
  5. Click on Add a new notification agent and select Script
  6. Specify the script folder where you placed the script and select the script file.

  7. Add an optional Description to identify the script.

  8. Go to Triggers, scroll down and select Recently Added.

  9. Go to Conditions, you can now specify when the script should get called.

  10. Set Media Type to the types you want to process, for example episode, movie, show and season.

  11. Exclude libraries without tmdb, tvdb, or Fanart IDs, or include only libraries where Posterizarr should create artwork.

  12. Next go to Arguments - Unfold Recently Added Menu and paste the following Argument, after that you can save it.

  13. Please do not change the Argument otherwise the script could fail.

Default Setup (Single Instance):

If you are using the default /posterizarr mount, paste this: 

<movie>RatingKey "{rating_key}" mediatype "{media_type}"</movie><show>RatingKey "{rating_key}" mediatype "{media_type}"</show><season>parentratingkey "{parent_rating_key}" mediatype "{media_type}"</season><episode>RatingKey "{rating_key}" parentratingkey "{parent_rating_key}" grandparentratingkey "{grandparent_rating_key}" mediatype "{media_type}"</episode>

Custom Path Setup (Multiple Instances):

If you are triggering a second Posterizarr instance (e.g., mounted as /posterizarr2), you must use the -p parameter right after each opening tag to define the target watcher directory: 

<movie>-p "/posterizarr2/watcher" RatingKey "{rating_key}" mediatype "{media_type}"</movie><show>-p "/posterizarr2/watcher" RatingKey "{rating_key}" mediatype "{media_type}"</show><season>-p "/posterizarr2/watcher" parentratingkey "{parent_rating_key}" mediatype "{media_type}"</season><episode>-p "/posterizarr2/watcher" RatingKey "{rating_key}" parentratingkey "{parent_rating_key}" grandparentratingkey "{grandparent_rating_key}" mediatype "{media_type}"</episode>


![backgroundtesting](images/Tautulli_Step4.png)

items.title: Tautulli Mode Windows
items.text:
Note

If Discord is configured it will send a Notification on each trigger.

This mode lets Tautulli trigger Posterizarr for a specific Plex item, such as a newly added show, movie, or episode.

  1. Open Tautulli and go to Settings - NOTIFICATION AGENTS
  2. Click on Add a new notification agent and select Script
  3. Specify the script folder of Posterizarr and select the script file.
  4. Set the script timeout to 0, which is unlimited. (The default is 30, which would kill the script before it finishes.)

  5. Add an optional Description to identify the script.

  6. Go to Triggers, scroll down and select Recently Added.

  7. Go to Conditions, you can now specify when the script should get called.

  8. Set Media Type to the types you want to process, for example episode, movie, show and season.

  9. Exclude libraries without tmdb, tvdb, or Fanart IDs, or include only libraries where Posterizarr should create artwork.

  10. Next go to Arguments - Unfold Recently Added Menu and paste the following Argument, after that you can save it.

  11. Please do not change the Argument otherwise the script could fail.
<movie>RatingKey "{rating_key}" mediatype "{media_type}"</movie><show>RatingKey "{rating_key}" mediatype "{media_type}"</show><season>parentratingkey "{parent_rating_key}" mediatype "{media_type}"</season><episode>RatingKey "{rating_key}" parentratingkey "{parent_rating_key}" grandparentratingkey "{grandparent_rating_key}" mediatype "{media_type}"</episode>

items.title: Tautulli Mode (Native Webhook)
items.text:
Recommended

This is the easiest way to set up Tautulli. It requires no custom scripts or volume mounts.

  1. Open Tautulli and go to Settings -> Notification Agents.
  2. Click Add a new notification agent and select Webhook.
  3. Configuration Tab:
    • Webhook URL: http://YOUR_POSTERIZARR_IP:8000/api/webhook/tautulli?api_key=YOUR_API_KEY
    • (Generate an API Key in Posterizarr settings under WebUI)
    • Webhook Method: POST
  4. Triggers Tab:
    • Check Recently Added.
  5. Data Tab:
    • Scroll down to Recently Added.
    • Paste the following into JSON Data: 
      {
    "RatingKey": "{rating_key}",
    "mediatype": "{media_type}",
    "parentratingkey": "{parent_rating_key}",
    "grandparentratingkey": "{grandparent_rating_key}"
}
  6. Click Save.

items.title: Sonarr/Radarr Mode Docker
items.text:
Warning

Arrs and Posterizarr must run as a container in Docker

Note

If Discord is configured it will send a Notification on each trigger.

Direct Upload Enforced in Trigger Modes

Arr trigger runs always force direct upload to your media server (Upload2Plex = true / Jellyfin / Emby), regardless of whether PlexUpload is set to false in your config.json.

This mode lets Sonarr or Radarr trigger Posterizarr for a specific Plex or Jellyfin item, such as a newly added show, movie, or episode.

For the legacy script-based setup, configure a script in Sonarr or Radarr as follows.

  1. Ensure you mount the Posterizarr directory to your Sonarr/Radarr container, as the script requires access to /posterizarr: 
    volumes:
  - "/opt/appdata/posterizarr:/posterizarr:rw"
    ⚠️ Note: This mount path is case-sensitive and must match exactly /posterizarr.
  2. Download ArrTrigger.sh from GitHub and place it in your Sonarr/Radarr script directory.
  3. For example, create a scripts folder in /opt/appdata/sonarr, resulting in the path: /opt/appdata/sonarr/scripts/ArrTrigger.sh
  4. Make sure to set executable permissions: chmod +x ArrTrigger.sh
  5. In Sonarr/Radarr, go to Settings → Connect.
  6. Click the + button and select Custom Script.
  7. Enter a name for the script.
  8. For Notification Triggers, select only On File Import.
  9. Under Path, browse to and select your ArrTrigger.sh script.
  10. Example: /config/scripts/ArrTrigger.sh
  11. With this setup, the Arr suite will create a file in /posterizarr/watcher whenever a file is imported.
  12. The file will be named like: recently_added_20250925114601966_1da214d7.posterizarr
  13. Posterizarr monitors this directory for files ending in .posterizarr.
  14. When such a file is detected, it waits up to 5 minutes(based on fileage), then reads the file and triggers a Posterizarr run for the corresponding item.

items.title: Sonarr/Radarr Mode (Native Webhook)
items.text:
Recommended

This method replaces the need for ArrTrigger.sh and works without complex volume mapping.

  1. Open Sonarr or Radarr.
  2. Go to Settings -> Connect.
  3. Click the + button and select Webhook.
  4. Name: Posterizarr
  5. On Import: Yes
  6. On Upgrade: Yes
  7. URL: http://YOUR_POSTERIZARR_IP:8000/api/webhook/arr?api_key=YOUR_API_KEY
    • (Generate an API Key in Posterizarr settings under WebUI)
  8. Method: POST
  9. Click Save.

items.title: Gather Logs Mode
items.text:
Run the script with the -GatherLogs flag. In this mode, the script collects logs, rotated logs, and database files into a single archive for troubleshooting.

Crucially, the script sanitizes these files before zipping them automatically masking API keys, tokens, PINs, and sensitive hostnames. The result is saved in the script root as posterizarr_support_<timestamp>.zip

!!! tip Use this when reporting bugs or requesting support. It allows you to share comprehensive debugging information with the developer without manually scrubbing your credentials or private links from the files.

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -GatherLogs

On docker this way:

docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -GatherLogs

items.title: Logo Updater Mode
items.text:
The Logo Updater Mode automatically scans your Plex libraries for missing ClearLogos (text-based title images), fetches them from online sources (TMDB, TVDB, Fanart.tv), and uploads them directly to your Plex server metadata.

Standard Update

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -LogoUpdater -LibraryName "Movies"

Revert Mode (Delete Posterizarr-added logos)

.\Posterizarr.ps1 -LogoRevert -LibraryName "Movies"

Parameters:

  • -LogoUpdater: Enable the logo search and upload process.
  • -LogoRevert: Search for logos previously added by Posterizarr (verified via fingerprinting) and unlinks them from Plex.
  • -ForceReplace: Overwrite existing logos even if they already exist in Plex.
  • -LogoExifCheck: Only replace existing logos if they lack Posterizarr EXIF metadata (e.g. default logos auto-selected by Plex). Existing logos created or uploaded by Posterizarr are skipped.
  • -LibraryName: Specify a single library name or use "all" to process all suitable Movie and TV libraries.

Tip

Fingerprinting & EXIF Checks: When running with -LogoExifCheck or in Revert mode, Posterizarr inspects the current logo for a metadata comment (created with posterizarr). Using -LogoExifCheck allows you to replace unwanted or wrong-language logos chosen by Plex's default agents while skipping logos Posterizarr already customized in prior runs.

In the WebUI, you can access this mode via the "Run Modes" tab. It provides a user-friendly interface to select libraries and toggle "Force Replace", "Only Replace Non-Posterizarr Logos (EXIF Check)", or "Revert" settings.

items.title: Manual Mode Logo Search
items.text:
In the WebUI's Manual Mode, you can use the "Browse Logos" button to search for ClearLogos/ClearArt directly from online providers.

  1. Open Manual Mode in the WebUI.
  2. Click "Browse Logos".
  3. Search for a movie or show.
  4. Select a logo to automatically use its URL as the title source.
  5. When you run the manual mode with a URL in the "Title Text" field, Posterizarr will download and use that image as a logo overlay on your poster.

items.title: Plex Sync Mode (WebUI & Scheduler)
items.text: The Plex Sync Mode is a dedicated, lightweight synchronization mechanism built directly into Posterizarr's WebUI backend. It allows you to selectively push generated artwork directly to your Plex server without running full PowerShell image generation cycles or triggering external scrapers.

items.title: Why Use Plex Sync Mode?
items.text:
• Lightweight & Fast: Pure Python execution utilizing PMS REST endpoints (/library/metadata/{rating_key}/posters and /arts). No ImageMagick overhead.
  • Change Tracking (Zero Redundant Uploads): Maintains an internal SQLite cache (database/plex_push_cache.db) recording file sizes, modification timestamps, and upload history. Assets that have not changed locally are skipped immediately.
  • Granular Control (Respects Kometa & Custom Workflows): You can select exactly which libraries (e.g. "Movies", "TV Shows", or "all") and which asset types to sync:
    • Collections: Collection posters (Assets/Collections/)
    • Posters: Movie and Show main posters (Assets/<Library>/<Item>/poster.*)
    • Seasons: TV Season posters (Assets/<Library>/<Item>/SeasonXX.*)
    • Title Cards: Episode title cards (Assets/<Library>/<Item>/<Item> - SxxExx.*)
    • Backgrounds: Fanart / Backdrops (Assets/<Library>/<Item>/background.*) If you manage movie posters with Kometa or PMM, you can enable Plex Sync exclusively for Collections without touching other media artwork.

items.title: Interactive Collection Explorer Diff & Push
items.text: Under Collection Builder (/media-server-collections): 1. Select your Plex server and library. 2. The UI automatically compares every local collection poster against the Plex server and labels it with real-time diff tags: - In Sync: Local poster matches Plex and was previously uploaded. - Update Ready: Local poster has been updated or edited locally and is ready to push. - Missing on Plex: Local collection poster exists on disk, but has not yet been pushed to Plex. - No Local Asset: Collection exists on Plex, but no local poster file was found in Assets/Collections/. 3. Use the LOCAL / SERVER toggle on each card to visually inspect the differences between your local asset and what is currently live on your Plex server. 4. Click Push to Plex on an individual collection card for instant 1-click upload, or click Push All Out-of-Sync in the toolbar to batch upload all pending collections concurrently.

items.title: Automated Scheduling
items.text:
In Scheduler (/scheduler): 1. Select Plex Sync (Lightweight) as the execution mode. 2. Select target library (All Libraries or a specific library). 3. Toggle which asset types to include using the interactive checkboxes. 4. Set your desired interval or cron schedule. 5. All sync activity is logged to UILogs/PlexSync.log and viewable in real-time in the WebUI Log Viewer.

Do not use Plex Sync schedule in combination with Kometa (Plex Meta Manager)!

If you run Kometa to manage posters, titlecards, or overlays, do not schedule a Plex Sync job for those same libraries or asset types.

Because Kometa applies its own overlays and metadata modifications directly to Plex, Posterizarr's Plex Sync will continuously detect that the live Plex artwork differs from your clean local assets and will repeatedly attempt to re-upload them. This triggers an endless overwrite cycle between Kometa and Posterizarr.

If you use Kometa, ensure that Plex Sync is only scheduled for asset types that Kometa does not touch (e.g. custom Collections only), or manage all uploads exclusively through Kometa.

items.title: Manual Assets Naming
items.text:
case-sensitive

Naming must follow these rules, including proper case sensitivity (uppercase and lowercase) in file/folder names; otherwise, the asset will not be picked up.

If you have Library Folders set to true, it will look like this:

Asset Naming Poster poster.* Season Season01.*Season02.*..... Season Special Season00.* TitleCard S01E01.*S01E02.*..... Background background.* EpisodeTemplate EpisodeTemplate.**Posterizarr will use this template file for all episodes during a run. SeasonTemplate SeasonTemplate.**Posterizarr will use this template file for all seasons during a run. 
├───Anime Shows
│   └───Solo Leveling (2024) [tvdb-389597]
│           poster.jpg
│           S01E01.jpg
│           Season01.jpg
│           background.jpg
│           EpisodeTemplate.jpg
│           SeasonTemplate.jpg

If you have Library Folders set to false, it will look like this:

Asset Naming Poster Solo Leveling (2024) [tvdb-389597].* Season Solo Leveling (2024) [tvdb-389597]_Season01.*Solo Leveling (2024) [tvdb-389597]_Season02.*..... Season Special Solo Leveling (2024) [tvdb-389597]_Season00.* TitleCard Solo Leveling (2024) [tvdb-389597]_S01E01.*Solo Leveling (2024) [tvdb-389597]_S01E02.*..... Background Solo Leveling (2024) [tvdb-389597]_background.* SeasonTemplate SeasonTemplate.**Posterizarr will use this template file for all seasons during a run. EpisodeTemplate EpisodeTemplate.**Posterizarr will use this template file for all episodes during a run. 
├───Anime Shows
│       Solo Leveling (2024) [tvdb-389597].jpg
│       Solo Leveling (2024) [tvdb-389597]_S01E01.jpg
│       Solo Leveling (2024) [tvdb-389597]_Season01.jpg
│       Solo Leveling (2024) [tvdb-389597]_background.jpg
│       EpisodeTemplate.jpg
│       SeasonTemplate.jpg

items.title: FAQ: Why the change to 127.0.0.1?
items.text:
Previously, the application listened on 0.0.0.0 by default, which means it was accessible from any device on your network. For security reasons, the default has been changed to 127.0.0.1 (localhost) for non-Docker installations. This ensures that the application is only accessible from the machine it's running on unless you explicitly choose to expose it.

Docker Users

This change does not affect Docker installations, which still default to 0.0.0.0 for ease of use within containers.

items.title: Troubleshooting: Cannot access the Web UI from another device?
items.text: By default, the app now listens on 127.0.0.1 (localhost) for security. If you are running this on a server and need to access it via your network, set the environment variable APP_HOST=0.0.0.0 before starting the application.

items.title: Recommended: Using a Reverse Proxy
items.text:
The most secure and recommended way to expose Posterizarr to your network or the internet is by using a reverse proxy (such as Nginx, Caddy, or Traefik).

When using a reverse proxy, you do not need to change APP_HOST. You can leave Posterizarr safely running on its default 127.0.0.1 (localhost) and configure your reverse proxy to forward traffic to Posterizarr's internal port. This is the recommended way because the application is still usable with 127.0.0.1 while securely handling external requests through the proxy.

items.title: How to set the APP_HOST environment variable
items.text: If you prefer to expose the application directly without a reverse proxy, how you set the APP_HOST environment variable depends entirely on how you are running the application. Since this change specifically affects those not using Docker (who want LAN access), here are the three most common ways to set it:

items.title: 1. Using a .env file
items.text:
Posterizarr supports .env files out of the box. This is the easiest way to manage your environment variables if you are not using a reverse proxy. Simply create a file named .env in the same folder as main.py with the following content:

APP_HOST=0.0.0.0
PORT=8000

items.title: 2. Persistent (System Service / Systemd)
items.text:
If you are running your app as a background service on a Linux server (like Ubuntu or Raspberry Pi OS), you likely have a .service file. You need to add the Environment line to your configuration:

  1. Edit the service file (usually in /etc/systemd/system/posterizarr.service).
  2. Add the variable under the [Service] section: 
    [Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /path/to/main.py
Environment="APP_HOST=0.0.0.0"
User=youruser
  3. Reload and restart: 
    systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart posterizarr

items.title: 3. Temporary (Command Line)
items.text:
If you are just testing the app or running it manually from a terminal, you can prepend the variable to the start command.

Linux / macOS: 

APP_HOST=0.0.0.0 python main.py

Windows (PowerShell): 

$env:APP_HOST="0.0.0.0"; python main.py

Windows (Command Prompt): 

set APP_HOST=0.0.0.0 && python main.py

items.title: Why 0.0.0.0 vs 192.168.x.x?
items.text:
• 0.0.0.0: Tells the app to listen on every available network interface (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, and Localhost). This is the easiest "catch-all" for users.
  • 192.168.1.50: Tells the app to only listen on that specific IP. If the server's IP changes (DHCP), the app will fail to start.

Verdict: Most users will prefer setting APP_HOST=0.0.0.0 as it is the most flexible for home server environments.

items.title: Docker
items.text:
• Docker-Compose Example File

  • Change RUN_TIME in yaml to your needs - You need to use 24H Time Format

    • The Script gets executed on the Times you specified
    • Before starting the scheduled run it checks if another Posterizarr process is running, if yes - the scheduled run will be skipped.
    • If set to disabled, the script will not run on a schedule but will still watch for file triggers and respond to manual triggers.
    • Required at disabled for the UI & if you want to set the schedules there.
  • Change volume and network to fit your environment (Make sure you have the same network as your plex container when you use local IP of plex)
  • Change TimeZone to yours, otherwise it will get scheduled to a different time you may want it to.
  • Add DISABLE_UI and set it to true if you want to disable the UI.
  • Change APP_PORT and set it to your prefered port (9000 also update it in compose ports block)
  • For external schedulers (for example Kubernetes CronJob), start the container with --run (or -Run) so Start.ps1 skips internal scheduling and executes immediately once.
  • You may also have to change user: "1000:1000" (PUID/PGID)
Optional: run a mode from the Docker terminal These commands are only needed if you deliberately want to control Posterizarr from a terminal. For everyday use, use the Web UI's **Run Modes** and **Scheduler** views. If you manually want to run the Script you can do it this way: **Automatic Mode:** 
docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1
**Testing Mode:** 
docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Testing
**Manual Mode (Interactive):** 
docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual
**Backup Mode:** 
docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Backup
**SyncJelly Mode:** 
docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -SyncJelly
**SyncEmby Mode:** 
docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -SyncEmby
**Poster reset Mode:** 
docker exec -it posterizarr pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -PosterReset -LibraryToReset "Test Lib"
!!! tip If you did not used `pwsh` on docker exec you can do it this way. Inside your `Unraid` or `Bash` or `Sh` console: 
pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1
pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Manual
pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Testing
pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -Backup
pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -SyncEmby
pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -SyncJelly
pwsh /app/Posterizarr.ps1 -PosterReset -LibraryToReset "Test Lib"

items.title: unRAID
items.text:
Tip

If you are an unRAID user, just use the Community app from @nwithan8 it is listed in Store.

  • Change RUN_TIME to your needs - You need to use 24H Time Format
    • Example: 06:00 or 06:00,14:00.....
  • AssetPath in config needs to be /assets not the path you entered.

items.title: Jellyfin
items.text:
In order to view the 16:9 episode posters without getting cropped to 3:2, you need to set a css.

#itemDetailPage .listItemImage-large {
  width: 16vw;
  height: 9vw;
}

items.title: Container Variables
items.text:
Variable Default Description RUN_TIME disabled A comma-separated list of 24-hour times (e.g., 03:00,15:00) for scheduled runs. If set to disabled, the UI will handle scheduling. APP_PORT 8000 The Web UI Port. DISABLE_UI false Set to true to disable the Web UI. ARR_WAIT_TIME 300 The time in seconds to wait after an Arr trigger to allow media servers (Jellyfin/Plex) to finish scanning. Advanced: one-shot containers and external schedulers

For one-shot runs without the internal scheduler loop, pass this startup arg:

--run

This is intended as a container startup argument.

Docker run example:

docker run --rm \
  -e TZ=Europe/Berlin \
  -e RUN_TIME=disabled \
  -e DISABLE_UI=true \
  -v /opt/appdata/posterizarr:/config:rw \
  -v /opt/appdata/posterizarr/assets:/assets:rw \
  ghcr.io/fscorrupt/posterizarr:latest \
  --run

Docker Compose example:

services:
  posterizarr:
    image: ghcr.io/fscorrupt/posterizarr:latest
    command: ["--run"]
    environment:
      - "RUN_TIME=disabled"
      - "DISABLE_UI=true"

Kubernetes CronJob container args example:

containers:
  - name: posterizarr
    image: ghcr.io/fscorrupt/posterizarr:latest
    args: ["--run"]

items.title: Scheduled Plex Image Cleanup
items.text:
Repeated custom poster/titlecard uploads can leave old, unselected images in Plex's metadata directory. Changing the selected poster does not necessarily remove those files.

Open Scheduler in the Web UI and add a Plex Image Cleanup task. Start with Read Only (Report) enabled, then review the report before choosing a quarantine or removal action. Quarantined copies can be reviewed under Asset Management > Plex Image Quarantine.

Posterizarr provides a separate Plex Image Cleanup scheduler task inspired by ImageMaid, by meisnate12 and the Kometa Team. ImageMaid in turn credits bullmoose20's Plex Bloat Fix. Selected-artwork protection in this integration adapts ImageMaid's MIT-licensed helpers. This is a limited image-cleanup integration, not the complete ImageMaid application.

items.title: Scheduled Or On Demand
items.text:
• No cleanup schedule is created or enabled by default.
  • Cleanup does not run on startup, after an upload, after overlay sync, or when previewing artwork.
  • Add a Plex Image Cleanup task in Scheduler. Use the play button beside any saved task to run it immediately with its saved options, even when the scheduler is disabled. To run it automatically, explicitly enable the scheduler.
  • On-demand cleanup uses the same Read Only setting, removal confirmation, age threshold, and safety checks as scheduled cleanup. Its progress opens in PlexImageCleanup.log.
  • Schedule it in a separate maintenance window after Posterizarr, Kometa, TitleCardMaker, and other artwork writers. In-app overlay work and queued requests exclude cleanup; overlay requests arriving during cleanup wait until it finishes. Existing scheduled tasks remain serialized by the scheduler. A loaded active Plex Sync worker also causes cleanup to skip.
  • API snapshot mode refuses to proceed while Plex reports active playback sessions. External tools and users changing artwork are not locked by Posterizarr; keep them idle throughout cleanup. Cleanup is not a transaction with the live Plex server.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
The Plex Data Directory is the Plex application-data directory containing Metadata, Cache, and Plug-in Support. It is not Posterizarr's clean-asset folder or the media-library directory.

For Docker, explicitly mount that directory into Posterizarr with :rw and configure /plex in the cleanup schedule. Leave the scheduler's Read Only (Report) switch enabled initially. It is on by default and prevents image changes even when the mount is writable. No mount is added automatically.

items.title: Docker Compose Examples
items.text:
Merge the relevant fragment into your existing posterizarr service, retaining its current environment entries and volumes. These are additions, not complete replacement Compose files.

Linux host:

services:
    posterizarr:
        environment:
            - "RUN_TIME=disabled"
        volumes:
            - "/path/to/Plex Media Server:/plex:rw"

Windows host with Plex container data:

services:
    posterizarr:
        environment:
            - "RUN_TIME=disabled"
        volumes:
            - 'C:\Docker\Plex\Library\Application Support\Plex Media Server:/plex:rw'

Replace the host path with the actual Plex data directory. API Export also requires Preferences.xml in that directory. A native Windows Plex installation without this file must use the stopped-Plex Local Database mode instead.

Keep Read Only (Report) enabled in the scheduler for the initial run. After reviewing the report, switch it off and choose Quarantine or Remove. With the :rw mount shown above, this does not require recreating the container. Ensure the container user has the required permissions; a writable mount alone does not grant filesystem permissions.

An optional Docker :ro mount provides an additional operating-system-level write block. The scheduler switch cannot change Docker mount permissions: if you deliberately use :ro, writable cleanup still requires changing the mount to :rw and recreating the container.

RUN_TIME=disabled disables the container's separate script timer so it does not compete with the UI scheduler. Neither the volume mount nor this setting creates or enables a cleanup schedule.

items.title: Scheduling With Plex Running
items.text:
Posterizarr does not start or stop Plex. Use Plex API Export for an unattended cleanup schedule while Plex stays running. Local Database mode requires you to stop Plex separately beforehand and is intended for offline maintenance.

  1. Configure the Plex URL/token in Posterizarr and mount the data directory as shown above.
  2. In Scheduler, select Plex Image Cleanup, set Plex Data Directory to /plex, and select Plex API Export.
  3. Keep Read Only (Report) enabled and the default seven-day minimum age for the first scheduled run.
  4. Choose a maintenance window with no playback or other artwork-writing jobs, add the schedule, and explicitly enable the UI scheduler.
  5. Review the cleanup log before disabling Read Only and selecting Quarantine or confirmed permanent removal.

Choose the snapshot source:

  • Plex API Export: Uses the existing configured Plex URL/token to download a fresh database export. The machineIdentifier returned by Plex's /identity endpoint must match either MachineIdentifier or ProcessedMachineIdentifier in the mounted Preferences.xml; Plex installations can expose the processed identifier instead of the raw value. This prevents cleaning one server's files using another server's selections. Redirects are not followed; oversized or ambiguous exports are rejected. Only the database member is read from ZIP exports, without extracting archive paths.
  • Local Database: Reads Plug-in Support/Databases/com.plexapp.plugins.library.db into a temporary SQLite backup. Plex must be stopped; the task refuses this mode if WAL/SHM files exist before or after the snapshot. There is no ignore-running override. On platforms without Preferences.xml, use this stopped-Plex mode.

The snapshot is queried read-only and removed when the task finishes. Posterizarr never edits the Plex database. Database exports are limited to 20 GiB.

If an identity mismatch remains after updating Posterizarr, verify that the configured Plex URL points to the server whose data directory is mounted at /plex. Compare only the two identifier attributes above with /identity; do not share the entire Preferences.xml, which can contain tokens and other private settings. Do not bypass the mismatch check.

items.title: Actions
items.text:
Read Only (Report) is enabled by default for new schedules and schedules that do not yet have a cleanup_read_only setting. While enabled, it locks the Action field to Report Only, clears permanent-removal confirmation, and forces Report mode in the backend even if a saved request contains Quarantine or Remove. Switching it off permits selecting a writable action; permanent removal still needs its separate confirmation.

Action Behavior Report Only Default. Counts eligible images and bytes without modifying images. Start here. Move to Quarantine Moves eligible images to a unique directory under database/plex-image-quarantine/ in Posterizarr's writable data directory. Original metadata-relative paths are preserved. Permanently Remove Deletes eligible images. Requires an explicit confirmation checkbox saved with that schedule. Cannot be undone.

Quarantine is not automatically purged. It removes files from Plex's metadata tree but does not reclaim total disk space when the quarantine is on the same filesystem. Review it before deleting it. To recover a quarantined image, stop artwork writers and copy it back under Plex's Metadata directory using its preserved relative path; existing files must not be overwritten blindly.

items.title: Delete Reviewed Quarantine Runs
items.text:
Open Asset Management > Plex Image Quarantine to see each cleanup run, its server-local creation time, file count, and stored size. This view is available only when Plex is enabled with a configured URL and either a Plex Image Cleanup schedule exists or previous cleanup data is present (a quarantine run, report, or nonempty cleanup log). It stays hidden for Emby/Jellyfin-only installations, even if old Plex cleanup data remains on disk. After checking the artwork in Plex and keeping any recovery buffer you need, use the trash icon beside that run and confirm Delete Permanently. Only that run's quarantined recovery copies are removed; other runs and active Plex artwork are not touched. Deletion cannot be undone.

This is an explicit user action, not an automatic purge or a manual execution of the scheduled Plex cleanup task. The scheduled task's Read Only setting does not prevent separately confirmed deletion of already quarantined copies. Deletion is disabled while cleanup or another purge is active, and linked/unreadable run contents are refused. The backend accepts only generated run IDs inside Posterizarr's database/plex-image-quarantine directory, never arbitrary filesystem paths.

The Remove action in the scheduler still deletes eligible images directly from Plex's metadata directory; it does not empty quarantine. Quarantined copies can alternatively be deleted through the host filesystem after review.

items.title: Protection Rules
items.text:
• Only valid JPEG/PNG/WebP images with extensionless SHA-1-style names under metadata Uploads directories are considered.
  • Selected posters, backgrounds, banners, clear logos, and square artwork are protected by every available supported metadata_items selection column, across the entire database.
  • Unsupported or empty metadata databases abort cleanup rather than assuming nothing is selected.
  • Provider/default images outside Uploads, Contents trees, uploaded themes, symlinks, junctions, and non-image files are excluded.
  • A grace period defaults to 7 days and cannot be shorter than 1 day.
  • Before moving/removing anything, the task refreshes selected-artwork data. Each candidate's path, size, modification timestamp, and selected status are rechecked. Files changed or selected since discovery are skipped.
  • The task does not clear PhotoTranscoder, empty Plex trash, clean bundles, optimize databases, or touch Posterizarr's original assets.

An older unselected upload may still be a useful alternative poster. Quarantine is preferable to permanent removal until you have reviewed a Report run.

items.title: Reports
items.text:
Each executed task creates UILogs/PlexImageCleanup.log at startup and appends timestamped progress for snapshot creation/download, selected-artwork protection, metadata scanning, and candidate processing. Long scans report progress periodically rather than once per image. The final JSON summary is appended to this log and written to UILogs/last_image_cleanup_report.json.

All UI logs and the latest cleanup report are preserved across backend and container restarts. In Docker, they live under /config/UILogs and survive container recreation when the same persistent /config volume is retained. Only when the next cleanup actually starts is PlexImageCleanup.log renamed to PlexImageCleanup.old.log, replacing the older backup. The new run writes a fresh active log, while the JSON report is replaced with the latest result. A skipped cleanup does not rotate the log.

The top navigation shows IMAGE CLEANUP, not Overlay Sync. Click that activity badge, or the log button beside the saved schedule, to open the cleanup live log. Cleanup has no Overlay Sync Stop action. Reports include action, candidate/changed counts and bytes, skipped files, errors, and the quarantine path when applicable. Busy skips are recorded by the scheduler.
